title: Ashgrove IncomeShield Guaranteed Lifetime Withdrawal Benefit — Benefit Base, Rider Fee and Lifetime Withdrawals
content:
## Rider provisions (Fixed Indexed Annuities tiers with the rider included)

**1. Benefit base.** On tiers where the guaranteed lifetime withdrawal benefit rider is included, the benefit base starts at the premiums received in the first contract year plus the benefit base bonus. On each of the first anniversaries — as many as the tier's number of roll-up anniversaries — before lifetime withdrawals start, the benefit base is credited a simple roll-up. Each roll-up credit is the tier's roll-up rate multiplied by the first-year premiums plus the benefit base bonus on them, rounded to the cent; being simple, it is figured on that same amount every time and never on earlier roll-up credits. The benefit base is that starting amount plus the roll-up credits, less proportional reductions already taken.

**2. Rider fee.** The rider fee is the tier's rider fee rate multiplied by the benefit base on the anniversary, rounded to the cent. It is deducted from the contract value on each anniversary and never exceeds the tier's highest rider fee.

**3. Election.** Lifetime withdrawals are started only on a lifetime income election signed by the owner and approved. The election is read from Ashgrove's service request record for that election — its request type, signed date and approved request status — before lifetime withdrawals start.

**4. Starting age and percentage.** Lifetime withdrawals may start once the covered person, or the younger of two covered spouses, has reached the tier's income age. The lifetime withdrawal percentage is taken from the lifetime withdrawal percentage table by that age on the start date, less the joint reduction for joint income, and is locked for life.

**5. Annual lifetime withdrawal amount.** The benefit base on the start date multiplied by the lifetime withdrawal percentage, rounded to the cent, payable at the frequency the owner elected. Withdrawals within it are free of surrender charge.

**6. Exhaustion.** When the contract value reaches zero through covered withdrawals and fees, payments continue for life from Ashgrove's guarantee and no further rider fee is charged; the contract is then in guaranteed payout status. An excess withdrawal that reduces the contract value to zero ends the rider without further payments.

### Worked example (hypothetical owner; Ashgrove IncomeShield 10 figures — benefit base bonus 15%, roll-up 8% on up to 10 anniversaries, rider fee 1.20%, income age 50, joint reduction 0.5 percentage point)

| Step | Figure |
|---|---|
| First-year premiums | 100000 |
| Benefit base bonus: 100000 multiplied by 15% | 15000.00 |
| Starting benefit base | 115000.00 |
| Each roll-up credit: 8% multiplied by 115000.00 | 9200.00 |
| Benefit base after three roll-up anniversaries, no reductions | 142600.00 |
| Rider fee on an anniversary where the benefit base is 142600.00: 1.20% of it | 1711.20 |

Lifetime withdrawals then start with a benefit base of 142600.00:

| Election | Age read | Percentage | Annual lifetime withdrawal amount |
|---|---|---|---|
| Single life, covered person 67 | 67, table row 65 | 5.5% | 7843.00 |
| Joint life, spouses 66 and 63 | 63, table row 60 | 5.0% less 0.5 point is 4.5% | 6417.00 |

After the start, the 4.5% or 5.5% does not change with later birthdays, and no further roll-up is credited.

### Points of judgement

- *Covered person aged 49 on the intended start date.* Below the income age of 50; lifetime withdrawals may not start yet.
- *Contract value reaches zero through scheduled lifetime withdrawals and rider fees.* Lifetime payments continue from the guarantee, with no further rider fee.
- *A withdrawal above the annual lifetime withdrawal amount brings the contract value to zero.* The rider ends and no further payments are made.
